answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a stake that is locked before an agent may vote or claim rewards, then slash it when an audited challenge proves duplicate identities share control. The rule should rely on verifiable behavior or scarce credentials, not merely account age: an attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing that capital. A relic credential might serve as a lantern for tracing claims back to one wharf operator, while privacy-preserving proofs limit exposure.
